bottom_line: In symptomatic chronic heart failure, n-3 PUFA 1 g daily versus placebo reduced all-cause death (adjusted HR 0.91 [95.5% CI 0.833–0.998]).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, n-3 PUFA 1 g daily was associated with a small reduction in all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.91 [95.5% CI 0.833–0.998]) and in death or cardiovascular admission (adjusted HR 0.92 [99% CI 0.849–0.999]); they do not show large absolute differences, with an absolute risk reduction for all-cause mortality of 1.8% (95% CI 0.3–3.9) and for mortality or admission for cardiovascular reasons of 2.3% (0.0–4.6).

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Italy comparing n-3 PUFA 1 g daily versus placebo.
major_points.quote: We undertook a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 326 cardiology and 31 internal medicine centres in Italy.

major_points.text: Patients with chronic heart failure NYHA class II–IV were enrolled irrespective of cause and left ventricular ejection fraction.
major_points.quote: We enrolled patients with chronic heart failure of New York Heart Association class II–IV, irrespective of cause and left ventricular ejection fraction

major_points.text: Primary endpoints were time to death and time to death or cardiovascular hospital admission; analysis was intention to treat.
major_points.quote: Primary endpoints were time to death, and time to death or admission to hospital for cardiovascular reasons. Analysis was by intention to treat.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was 27% vs 29% with an adjusted HR 0.91 (95.5% CI 0.833–0.998).
major_points.quote: 955 (27%) patients died from any cause in the n-3 PUFA group and 1014 (29%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0·91 [95·5% CI 0·833–0·998], p=0·041).

major_points.text: Composite of death or cardiovascular admission occurred in 57% vs 59% with adjusted HR 0.92 (99% CI 0.849–0.999).
major_points.quote: 1981 (57%) patients in the n-3 PUFA group and 2053 (59%) in the placebo group died or were admitted to hospital for cardiovascular reasons (adjusted HR 0·92 [99% CI 0·849–0·999], p=0·009).

major_points.text: Gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction and were similar between groups.
major_points.quote: In both groups, gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction (96 [3%] n-3 PUFA group vs 92 [3%] placebo group).

absolute_effects.quote: 955 (27%) patients died from any cause in the n-3 PUFA group and 1014 (29%) in the placebo group

absolute_effects.text: Death or admission for cardiovascular reasons: 1981 (57%) vs 2053 (59%).
absolute_effects.quote: 1981 (57%) patients in the n-3 PUFA group and 2053 (59%) in the placebo group died or were admitted to hospital for cardiovascular reasons

absolute_effects.text: Absolute risk reductions: 1.8% (95% CI 0.3–3.9) for all-cause mortality and 2.3% (0.0–4.6) for mortality or admission for cardiovascular reasons.
absolute_effects.quote: the risk reduction for all-cause mortality was 1·8% (95% CI 0·3–3·9) and for mortality or admission for cardiovascular reasons was 2·3% (0·0–4·6)

absolute_effects.text: Numbers needed to treat: 56 to avoid one death and 44 to avoid one event like death or cardiovascular admission (median 3.9 years).
absolute_effects.quote: In absolute terms, 56 patients needed to be treated for a median duration of 3·9 years to avoid one death or 44 to avoid one event like death or admission to hospital for cardiovascular reasons.

subgroups.text: Subgroup analyses were prespecified for age, LVEF, cause of heart failure, NYHA class, diabetes, and baseline total cholesterol.
subgroups.quote: assessed in subgroups of patients deﬁned according to age (above vs below the median value); left ventricular function (LVEF >40% vs ≤40%); cause of heart failure (ischaemic vs non-ischaemic); functional capacity (NYHA class II vs III or IV); presence of diabetes (yes vs no); and baseline total cholesterol concentrations (above vs below the median value).

subgroups.text: No significant interactions were recorded for subgroup analyses.
subgroups.quote: We recorded no signiﬁcant interactions for any subgroup analysis.

subgroups.text: Composite endpoint subgroup result in diabetes: 623/992 (62.8%) vs 660/982 (67.2%), HR 0.89 (0.80–0.99).

harms.text: Gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction (3% vs 3%).
harms.quote: In both groups, gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction (96 [3%] n-3 PUFA group vs 92 [3%] placebo group).

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women aged 18 years or older with clinical evidence of heart failure of any cause, classified as NYHA class II–IV.

inclusion_criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction had to have been measured within 3 months before enrolment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: provided that they had had their LVEF measured within 3 months before enrolment.

inclusion_criteria.text: If LVEF was greater than 40%, at least one hospital admission for heart failure in the preceding year was required.
inclusion_criteria.quote: When LVEF was greater than 40%, the patient had to have been admitted at least once to hospital for heart failure in the preceding year to meet the inclusion criteria.

analysis_methods.quote: Analysis was by intention to treat.

analysis_methods.text: Main analysis used Cox proportional hazards models.
analysis_methods.quote: To estimate treatment eﬀect, the main analysis was undertaken by ﬁtting Cox proportional hazards models

analysis_methods.text: Adjusted analyses used covariates unbalanced at baseline (p<0.1), prespecified in protocol.
analysis_methods.quote: adjusted for the variables that were unbalanced between randomised groups (p<0·1). Although only adjusting for covariates that are signiﬁcantly out of baseline balance at p<0·1 is not recommended statistical practice, we did prespecify this approach in the protocol

analysis_methods.text: Different significance levels were used for the two co-primary endpoints (0.045 and 0.01).
analysis_methods.quote: with the ﬁrst (time to death) tested at a two-sided signiﬁcance level of 0·045 and the second (time to death or admission for cardiovascular reasons) at a signiﬁcance level of 0·01.
